summary: Accounting AC-10 HTTP runtime adapter foundation binds existing accounting API DTOs to the repo-native Hyper router/middleware foundation with OpenAPI-aligned JSON responses and explicit non-deployed runtime non-claims.

findings: Runtime adapter remains a thin boundary: parse DTO JSON, call accounting app functions, serialize response.
No ledger storage, payment execution, filing rails, Payroll call, Workflow execution, or audit emitter was added.
Uses the repo-native Hyper/router/middleware seam and mirrors HR/payroll runtime patterns for consistency.
Exports bounded server config and route manifest for future per-cell runtime mounting.

findings: Positive route dispatch and negative parse/domain errors are tested through transport-neutral HttpRequest/HttpResponse.
The crate exposes named route constants, route manifest, server config, router builder, chain builder, and dispatch helper.
Accounting runtime tests, accounting package-group tests/clippy, 15-package enterprise regression tests/clippy, fmt, Accounting OpenAPI semver, data_class scan, and quality-marker scan passed.

alternatives_named: bind accounting DTOs to the existing Hyper router foundation
F6_alternatives.selected_rationale: Repo-native Hyper router binding advances runtime readiness without adding framework dependency surface or overclaiming deployment.
rejected_reasons: A new framework would violate the established Hyper backbone.
Live deployment requires auth, ledger storage, Workflow, SLO, filing/payment rails, and ops evidence not present in this slice.

findings: Invalid JSON and invalid financial-domain commands return validation envelopes instead of panicking.
Server config fixes a 64 KiB body cap and short header/keepalive timeouts for future listener mounting.

F8_performance.regression_baseline: No deployed listener exists; tests exercise in-process router dispatch over fixed DTO bodies.

findings.summary: Route dispatch is bounded by shared router matching and fixed-size JSON payload handling; no I/O loops or storage calls are introduced.

findings: Public runtime response and route-manifest fields carry data_class annotations.
Health response explicitly marks deployed listener, storage, Workflow execution, filing rails, payment execution, and Payroll calls false.
The change is additive: one accounting runtime crate, catalog row, workspace membership, spec/tasks/evidence updates, and no migrations or external resources.
Route manifest names operation IDs and data-class classifications for future telemetry labels.
Health response exposes router-ready status and non-claim booleans without runtime emission claims.
Accounting AC-10 and D-10 record the runtime adapter foundation and keep deploy/storage/Workflow/filing/payment/Payroll as future slices.

M1_challenge_assumption.premise_stated: An accounting HTTP runtime foundation can land before cloud integration if it stays router-only and does not claim deployed ledger, filing, payment, or Workflow runtime.
M1_challenge_assumption.premise_evidence_ref: specs/microservices/accounting.json AC-10 and runtime health non-claim tests
M1_challenge_assumption.do_nothing_consequence: Accounting would keep DTO/OpenAPI contracts but lack executable route bindings for later runtime/server mounting.
M1_challenge_assumption.upstream_fix_rejection_reason: Shared Hyper foundation already exists; the missing seam is accounting-specific route binding.

findings: This completes first-pass router-ready runtime foundations for HR, Payroll, and Accounting while preserving honest non-claims.
Names follow accounting journal, payroll posting, VAT workflow, runtime adapter, route manifest, and OpenAPI operation vocabulary.
Accounting spec, OpenAPI meta, plan, todo, evidence, catalog, and audit-chain references were updated.
Runtime-specific code lives in a new accounting runtime crate; API DTOs and app/domain crates remain unchanged.
No new HTTP framework, storage repository, Workflow client, Payroll client, payment rail, filing transport, audit emitter, or deployment artifact was introduced.

No new third-party dependencies were added; runtime uses existing workspace serde/serde_json and repo-native HTTP foundation crates, and dependency-rationales allow-list was updated for adapter-layer use.
Responses use camelCase JSON and align to existing AccountingAccepted and VatWorkflowPlanResponse OpenAPI shapes; OpenAPI metadata records the runtime adapter addition.
Handlers perform deterministic parse -> app call -> JSON response flow with explicit 400/202/200 status mapping.
